aboutHeading: How to add subtitles to a video
aboutSteps: Choose an MP4, MKV, WebM or MOV video, select the spoken language or use automatic detection, then generate subtitles from the audio. Play the video to check the timing and edit any words the model misheard. You can also open an existing SRT file or enter subtitles by hand.
exportHeading: Embed subtitles in MP4 or MKV
exportDetails: The exported video contains a selectable subtitle track that viewers can turn on or off in compatible players. Video and audio are copied without re-encoding. If your video codecs are incompatible with MP4, try MKV. Download SRT if you want to reuse the subtitles in a video editor or upload them separately.
privacyHeading: Automatic captions with local speech recognition
privacyDetails: The first transcription downloads a Whisper speech recognition model. Inference uses WebGPU when available and can fall back to your CPU. Video, audio and subtitle edits stay in your browser. Review automatically generated captions for names, punctuation and timing before sharing.
